scope: Aggregate (group-level) holdings of BlackRock and Vanguard in the ten largest NIFTY 50 companies by index weight — Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys, Bharti Airtel, ITC, TCS, Larsen & Toubro, Axis Bank, State Bank of India — computed bottom-up from the funds' own published holdings files, and compared with the named ≥1% lines in the companies' SEBI shareholding-pattern filings recorded in holders.json. BlackRock: eight US-listed iShares ETFs (INDA, IEMG, EEM, ACWI, INDY, IXUS, ACWX, EMXC; daily holdings CSVs as of 2026-09-24) summed per company and divided by shares outstanding (primary filings for RIL, HDFC Bank, ITC, Bharti Airtel; screener.in equity-capital/face-value for ICICI Bank, Infosys, TCS, L&T, Axis Bank, SBI). This is a LOWER BOUND: Ireland-domiciled iShares UCITS ETFs, BlackRock Global Funds active sub-funds, institutional index mandates and ADR-channel holdings are not summed. Vanguard: fund-level summation was NOT possible (Vanguard's sites serve no holdings endpoint through this proxy; SEC N-PORT XML on www.sec.gov/Archives returns 403), so Vanguard is recorded as the named-line lower bound from the five primary filings (2.44% in HDFC Bank; no named line elsewhere). NBIM: two nbim.no probes returned a JavaScript shell and a 404; NBIM is compared using its named lines only. Also records the rule (1% naming threshold, fund-level registration) that explains why BlackRock's aggregate is invisible in filings that name smaller holders. Leaves out: the other 40 NIFTY 50 constituents; any per-fund voting/stewardship analysis; adviser mandates and rule-change history (companion files).

narratives.strongestCase: Computed bottom-up, BlackRock's presence is larger than the Indian filings make it look: eight US-listed iShares ETFs alone hold 1.0–1.8% of seven of the ten largest NIFTY 50 companies (Infosys 1.78%, HDFC Bank 1.75%, ICICI Bank 1.73%, Axis Bank 1.69%, L&T 1.18%, Bharti Airtel 1.09%, Reliance 1.01%) — about US$9.9bn of these ten stocks at the funds' own valuation — and that is before Ireland-domiciled iShares funds, active BlackRock funds, institutional mandates and ADRs, which plausibly at least double it. Vanguard's two named funds hold 2.44% of HDFC Bank, more than BlackRock's eight-fund total there. Both are invisible or nearly so in the filings because disclosure is per registered fund at a 1% threshold, so the public record understates them. And BlackRock has a domestic foothold through the 50:50 JioBlackRock ventures (holders:c019).
narratives.strongestCounter: Even the most generous reading does not approach ownership or control. The eight-fund BlackRock aggregate is 0.5–1.8% per company — 2–7% of the total foreign-portfolio holding in each, and 3–27× smaller than LIC's single line where LIC is named (RIL 6.88%, HDFC Bank 4.77%, ITC 15.69%, SBI 9.38%). The largest foreign stakes in the ten are strategic/FDI holders — BAT 22.91% of ITC, Singtel's Pastel 7.49% of Bharti Airtel — not passive managers. Promoters and the President of India hold 50.48% of RIL and 57.43% of SBI. The holdings are mechanical index weights: INDA, IEMG, EEM, ACWI, INDY, IXUS, ACWX and EMXC each hold every constituent at roughly its MSCI/NIFTY weight, so the aggregate is a consequence of India's index weight (India ≈ 2.1% of NBIM's equity book, for comparison), not of decisions about these companies. Vanguard's aggregate is unquantified here, so 'BlackRock and Vanguard' is half-measured, and the half that is measured is small.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Toward 'contested': a consolidated group-level disclosure (SEBI Aug 2023 granular FPI norms) or an N-PORT/UCITS summation showing the BlackRock or Vanguard complex above ~5% of several of these companies, or documented voting/engagement conduct in Indian companies that goes beyond published stewardship policy. Toward 'debunked' beyond the present 'unsupported': the full-complex numbers landing where the iShares-only lower bound suggests (2–4%), confirming the index-weight explanation.

symmetryCheck: The same bottom-up lens was applied to the controls to the extent sources allowed. Vanguard: only named lines (HDFC Bank 2.44% via two funds) — larger than BlackRock's eight-fund aggregate in the same company (1.75%), and Vanguard's per-fund concentration makes it more, not less, visible than BlackRock. NBIM: named at 1.34% (HDFC Bank) and 1.06% (Bharti Airtel) — smaller than BlackRock's unnamed aggregate in both (1.75%, 1.09%), yet the one that appears by name; nbim.no data itself not retrievable. GIC: named at 2.17% (HDFC Bank) and 1.22% (Bharti Airtel) — larger than BlackRock's aggregate in both. LIC (domestic control): 4.77–15.69% single lines, 3–27× the BlackRock aggregate. Strategic foreign holders (BAT 22.91% of ITC, Pastel/Singtel 7.49% of Bharti Airtel) dwarf every passive manager. Run on the controls, the lens produces the same shape — passive managers at 1–2.5% per company, sovereign funds at 1–2%, domestic LIC far above — which is a finding about index investing, not about BlackRock. The one asymmetry the lens does expose is disclosure: multi-fund managers (BlackRock) are systematically less visible than single-vehicle holders (NBIM, GIC) of the same or smaller size.
